messages.author: 637c00088bba8c56
messages.subject: Controlling levels in geom_density2d
parts:
How can I feed this geom with information levels at which to draw
contour lines? Basically what I want is to re-draw the contour plot
below using ggplot:

attach(geyser)
f1 <- kde2d(duration[-272], duration[-1], n = 50)
contour(f1, xlab = "previous duration", ylab = "duration", levels =
c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2) )
detach(geyser)

p <- ggplot(geyser)
p <- p + geom_density2d(aes(x = duration[-272], y = duration[-1]))
print(p)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Controlling levels in geom_density2d
parts:
Hi:

You could do something like this:

library(MASS)
f1 <- with(geyser, kde2d(duration[-272], duration[-1], n = 50))
f2 <- data.frame(expand.grid(x = f1$x, y = f1$y), z = as.vector(f1$z))
> dim(f2)
[1] 2500    3

p <- ggplot(f2)
p + stat_contour(aes(x = x, y = y, z = z), breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2))


Unlike contour plots in base graphics, text representation of contour
levels is not provided by default in ggplot2.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Controlling levels in geom_density2d
parts:
Hi,

geom_contour accepts breaks parameter and also stats like this:

ggplot(geyser) + geom_contour(aes(x = duration[-272], y =
duration[-1]), stat="density2d", breaks=0:2/10)
ggplot(geyser) + geom_contour(aes(x = duration[-272], y =
duration[-1]), stat="density2d", breaks=0:20/100)

--
Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com>

Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology,
The University of  Tokyo, Japan.
